title: Build a Harvest alternative with Claude: free timesheets spec, 21/21 checks passed
description:
Claude built a Harvest alternative from one Markdown spec: all 21 acceptance checks passed in a real browser, along with 123 automated tests.
The test build also exposed 21 gaps in the spec, and every one is now fixed.

We gave Claude one Markdown spec for weekly timesheets for teams of 5 to 100 people and had it build the tool in four phases: people, projects and sign-in; My week with submit and withdraw; approvals, rates and budgets; and reminders, reports and the approved-hours export. The core rule is the lock: approving a week locks it and copies each entry's rate onto the entry, so when the Website redesign rate goes from $150 to $160 an hour, Lee's approved weeks still bill at $150. The gaps included a sign-in limited to the company email domain with no setting to hold the domain, an hours field the spec described like a picker while a check typed 1:40 and expected a refusal, and export notes starting with "=" that would run as spreadsheet formulas. What passed, what broke, what we didn't test, and when Harvest is still the better buy.

Ten seats on Enterprise, billed annually, come to $1,680 a year.
